verdict.line: You lose if you let Gnar poke you to half HP before level 6 engages land; you win if you force all-ins while his E (Hop/Crunch) is down.

brief.thesis: This is a 44.1% matchup over 68 games despite Kled's 49.7% baseline in lane, because Gnar's ranged Q (Boomerang Throw) and Rage meter dictate when trades happen. Kled has no way to close the gap before level 3 jousts come online, so the first 0-2 levels are about minimizing poke, not fighting for it.

theirWindow.when: Rage bar is near max, E up
theirWindow.what: He's about to transform into Mega Gnar and get Wallop's stun plus a bigger Hop/Crunch landing. Back off cooldown walls and don't commit E (Jousting) into a stun you can't see coming.

yourWindow.what: OP.GG's own read confirms it: close the gap and dump W (Violent Tendencies) auto-resets now, since he has no escape to disengage your dash chain.

powerCurve.note: Boomerang Throw pokes for free, you have no gap-closer
Mega Gnar transform adds Wallop stun threat
Titanic Hydra wave clear and all-in power online

start.why: 76% pick rate and 49.1% win over 57 games; the extra sustain and damage keep you alive through early Boomerang Throw poke.

boots.why: 83.6% pick rate; Gnar's autos and Boomerang Throw are physical, and Steelcaps' auto-attack reduction cuts the poke that defines his early lead.

core.why: First item in the top two build paths (14.9% and 10.6% pick); the wave-clear and bonus HP let you shove and punish Hop/Crunch cooldowns.
Core second item in the top build path; armor shred matters since Mega Gnar stacks tankiness.
Third item in the 14.9% pick path; the HP and bonus damage scale your all-in once Mega Gnar is online.

situational.when: you're ahead on waves and want to push structures instead of Black Cleaver
you need burst-damage survivability against his Mega Gnar all-in
he lands GNAR! wall-stuns consistently and you need tenacity over armor

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained stacking damage rewards the extended trades Kled wants once E (Jousting) is online, and the healing offsets Boomerang Throw chip damage.

summoners.why: 67.5% pick rate at 51.8% win; Ignite punishes his low early HP pool when you land a jousting trade before he can disengage.

playing.title: Hold E until level 3
playing.detail: Jousting is your only gap-closer against his 1100-range Boomerang Throw; don't waste it approaching before it's live.

playing.title: Track his Rage bar, not just HP
playing.detail: A near-full Rage meter means his next ability triggers Mega Gnar, adding Wallop's stun. Disengage before that threshold instead of after.

playing.title: All-in only when E is down
playing.detail: Hop/Crunch is his only escape pre-6; once it's on cooldown (22/19.5/17/14.5/12s), commit W (Violent Tendencies) and E (Jousting) together.

playing.title: Save Pocket Pistol for dismount
playing.detail: When Skaarl dies, Q becomes Pocket Pistol — a ranged knockback blast that restores courage. Use it to disengage, not chase, since it knocks you backward.

playing.title: Respect GNAR! near walls
playing.detail: At level 6+, his R throws you in a direction and stuns if you hit a wall. Don't fight with your back to terrain once he's transformed.

playing.title: Use R (Chaaaaaaaarge!!!) to punish backline poke
playing.detail: At 3500 range, your ultimate closes gaps he can't escape once his E is down — align it with teamfights, not lane skirmishes.

playing.title: Shove waves after level 11
playing.detail: Titanic Hydra's wave clear lets you force tempo; a shoved wave limits his Boomerang Throw poke angles and sets up jungle ganks.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the lane-timing and mechanical reasoning are my own tactical read, not sourced from that data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Mega Gnar’s GNAR! (R) – Wallop (W) stun combo. Close in to deal damage once Hop/Crunch (E) is on cooldown.
